answer: Agents gain influence only after completing tasks whose results are independently verified by randomly assigned peers; each verified task requires a stake locked in a vault and risks slashing for fraud. A Sybil attacker can create many identities cheaply, but cannot multiply influence without funding separate stakes and producing useful work that survives review. The kernel selects reviewers unpredictably, while a lantern audit exposes suspicious clusters of mutually approving identities, making coordinated fake accounts costly to sustain.
